summary: A person at a client becomes a signed-in principal of the organization through a new ClientMembership row — never a role on Membership — so a member of staff can address a request to them and watch it answered in the product. Six pieces: (1) one additive migration adding ClientMembership and RequestNotification and four nullable columns; (2) the shared validation half — CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES, a ClientCapability union of its own, the `client` addressee kind and the `client` invitation role; (3) principal resolution on the session plus the rule that a client principal is answered 404 on every organization route except the requests list, their own request, its answer/decline/message routes, and create and grant (which answer named 403s); (4) the contacts routes on a client, the client branch of invitation acceptance, and the mirrored refusal that stops a client contact being invited to staff; (5) client-addressed requests end to end — the project rules, the topic audience rule, party/answer/decline/message/grant; (6) the notification port: one outbox row per recipient written in the transaction that wrote the event, delivered after the commit by an adapter that delivers nothing. The web half gives the contact a shell that is the requests screens with the rest of the navigation withheld, and gives staff an addressee-kind control in the new-request modal and a contacts section on client detail.

tasks.title: Schema and the one migration — ClientMembership, RequestNotification, four nullable columns
tasks.description: Add `ClientMembership` (id, accountId @unique FK Cascade, organizationId FK Cascade, clientId FK Cascade, status @default("active"), invitedByMembershipId? FK SetNull, joinedAt, removedAt?, removedByAccountId? FK SetNull; @@index([organizationId, status]), @@index([clientId, status])) and `RequestNotification` (id, organizationId FK Cascade, requestId FK Cascade, eventId FK Cascade, recipientKind, recipientId with NO foreign key, channel @default("none"), providerKey?, providerRef?, status @default("pending"), attempts Int @default(0), lastError?, handledAt?, createdAt; @@unique([eventId, recipientKind, recipientId]), @@index([organizationId, status, createdAt])). Add four nullable columns: Invitation.clientId (FK Client, SetNull), Request.assigneeClientMembershipId (FK, SetNull), RequestMessage.authorClientMembershipId (FK, SetNull), RequestEvent.actorClientMembershipId (FK, SetNull). No column changes type or nullability, nothing is renamed or dropped, no NOT NULL is added to an existing table, and no data is backfilled. `recipientId` deliberately carries no FK so a notification survives the principal it points at being removed.

migration.note: One migration. `infra/deploy.sh` registers the migrate task definition and runs `infra/migrate.sh` (lines 175-185) and only then `tf apply`s the services (lines 187-192), so the schema changes while the PREVIOUS image is still serving; the migrate step is skipped entirely when `api` is not among the changed services. Two unreferenced tables and four nullable columns are invisible to that code, which is what makes the window safe.

concurrency.lock: none at DDL time; the constraints are the concurrency mechanism — `ClientMembership.accountId @unique` for two concurrent accepts, `RequestNotification @@unique([eventId, recipientKind, recipientId])` for a replayed event

tasks.title: packages/validation — CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES, the client capability list, the client addressee kind and the client invitation role
tasks.description: Add `CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES` as a NEW export in packages/validation/src/index.ts (emailInvalid, alreadyLinked, alreadyRemoved, principalConflict, clientCannotCreate) with the text from the Error Messages table verbatim. Add three NEW KEYS to the existing `REQUEST_MESSAGES` const in place — clientProjectRequired, clientProjectMismatch, notOnProject — never a second export. Add a `ClientCapability` union and a flat readonly `CLIENT_CAPABILITIES` list holding exactly `read-own-requests`, `answer-request`, `decline-request`, `post-request-message`: values that belong to NEITHER staff union, so `MemberCapability` gains nothing, `Capability` gains nothing, `ROLE_CAPABILITIES` gains no row and `CAPABILITY_MATRIX` gains no column. Widen `REQUEST_ASSIGNEE_KINDS` to ['member','client'] and give `validateRequestAssignee`/`validateNewRequest` the client branch: `assigneeClientMembershipId` required when the kind is `client` (REQUEST_MESSAGES.assigneeInvalid), `projectId` required when the kind is `client` (REQUEST_MESSAGES.clientProjectRequired), an unknown kind still refused. Widen the invitation role set so `client` is accepted for a contact invitation without letting it be assigned through the staff invite body — `isValidRole` governs the staff-facing set and the client value must not become assignable there. This task adds NO role-keyed lookup for a client: a principal-kind resolver is the caller's job (T3, T7).

tasks.title: The principal — resolution on the session, sign-in, the identity answer, and 404 on every other organization route
tasks.description: Resolve the principal kind from the database on every request and put it on the request alongside the session — the cookie's fields do not change and no cookie minted before this spec becomes invalid. `SessionGuard` already re-reads the account for the security stamp, so the memberships and client memberships are read in that same query rather than in a second one. Sign-in: resolve the principal by REQ-03-002's decision table (staff row wins; an active client row alone resolves the client principal and issues the cookie for that client's organization; every other cell is the existing `AUTH_MESSAGES.deactivated`, still decided BEFORE the password compare so no answer becomes a password oracle). `GET /api/me`: one shape for both principals — `principal: "member"|"client"`, `client: {id,name}|null`, `role` null for a client — adding members and removing none. REQ-03-019: a client principal is answered a bare 404 on every organization route except the seven the spec names; implement it at the one choke point every `api/organizations/:orgId` controller already shares (`OrgScopeGuard`), with an explicit opt-in decorator on the seven exempt handlers, so a route added later is refused by default. Create and grant are the two exceptions that answer 403 — their bodies are decided in the service (T5), because REQ-03-027's ordering is part of the rule. Roles are in transition: any staff role read on this path goes through `normalizeRole()` (`packages/validation/src/roles.ts`), and a client principal must reach NEITHER `hasCapability` (which would normalize its absent role to `viewer` and hand back a set including ViewOwnRequests) NOR `can` — REQ-03-017 is an ordering rule and the kind is asked first.

concurrency.lock: none — these are reads. The stamp comparison in SessionGuard is the revocation mechanism and is re-read per request

tasks.title: Client contacts — invite, list, remove — and the two-ended principal conflict on invitation
tasks.description: Three routes on the client: POST contacts (201), GET contacts (200), DELETE contacts/{contactId} (200). Capability is decided IN THE SERVICE and a caller lacking it gets a bare 404 — never a 403 naming the capability — reusing the discipline of `ClientsService.requireManageCapability` (:360) and `requireViewCapability` (:369); the staff role goes through `normalizeRole()` inside `can`, so the legacy `member` value is refused exactly as `user` is. Queries scope by `session.organizationId`, never the path parameter. Invite: refuse an archived client 400 CLIENT_MESSAGES.clientArchived; refuse an address already holding a ClientMembership at another client of the organization, or an active one at this client, 409 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.alreadyLinked whatever the other row's status; write an `Invitation` carrying the client's id and role `client`, invalidating every other pending invitation for that address in the organization — staff or client — in the same transaction, which is the `updateMany` at invitations.service.ts:105 extended, not a second mechanism. Reuse the existing token: SHA-256 hash, seven-day expiry, the same accept screen and the mail sink's existing `invitation` message type. Accept: the `client` branch creates ONE active ClientMembership or returns the account's existing row to `active` with removedAt/removedByAccountId cleared, writes NO Membership, and answers redirectTo `/requests`; an account already holding an active Membership or an active ClientMembership of any organization is 409 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.principalConflict with nothing written. REQ-03-042 mirrors it at the other end: a STAFF invitation written for, or accepted by, an account holding an active ClientMembership of any organization is 409 principalConflict, writing neither the invitation nor the Membership — the existing duplicate check at invitations.service.ts:90 reads staff rows only and must not be relied on. Remove: status → removed with removedAt and removedByAccountId, and `Account.securityStamp` rotated IN THE SAME TRANSACTION so there is no window in which the row is removed and the stamp is not; removing an already-removed contact is 409 alreadyRemoved. `status` on the list row is `invited` while a pending invitation exists with no accepted row, `active` once accepted, `removed` after a removal.

concurrency.lock: one transaction per write. `ClientMembership.accountId @unique` is the backstop for two concurrent accepts of the same address; the removal's status write and the securityStamp rotation share one transaction (REQ-03-006); the invitation's supersession `updateMany` and its `create` share one transaction (REQ-03-011), which is the shape invitations.service.ts:105 already uses

tasks.title: Client-addressed requests — create rules, party, list, transitions and the thread
tasks.description: Create: REQ-03-027 first — a client principal is 403 CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.clientCannotCreate BEFORE the route consults any capability, so a client never receives REQUEST_MESSAGES.createForbidden (the sentence written for a viewer) and a malformed body is not answered as a validation error. Then the existing order, which the answers make observable and which the current code already follows: body shape together, then the topic row (REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicUnavailable for archived / another organization's / no row, audience never compared), then the audience comparison (topicAudienceMismatch, all four cells of the decision table), then the addressee (`assigneeClientMembershipId` naming a contact of the CALLER's organization — an unknown id and one of another organization are alike and answer a bare 404, and only then is a removed contact of the caller's own organization 400 assigneeInactive), then the project last (clientProjectRequired when absent, clientProjectMismatch when not linked to the addressee's client, notOnProject when the requester holds no ProjectMember row — an admin is NOT carved out). Read: a client principal is a party to a request whose addressee they are, and to nothing else — a request they are not the addressee of is 404, identical to one that does not exist. List: a client principal receives only requests addressed to them for `scope=mine`, `scope=all` and no scope alike (200, never the 403 a member without view-all-requests gets), the response carries NO `vacation` member, `counts.waitingOnMe` is the count of non-terminal requests addressed to them, and any other `scope` value is the 400 validation_error every principal receives, decided before the caller's kind is looked at. Answer, decline and message keep the two tests they apply to a member — party, and for answer and decline the addressee — evaluated against the row re-read with FOR UPDATE (`lockRequest`, :848), whichever kind the actor is; the events and the decline's reason message carry `actorKind`/`authorKind` of `client` and the client membership id, with display names still snapshotted into the label columns. Grant is 403 REQUEST_MESSAGES.notYoursToGrant for a client principal. A request whose addressee has since been removed reports its assignee inactive and is cancelled by nothing. The serializer's `assignee` member gains `kind: "client"`, the contact's display name and `clientName`, and never the contact's email address.

concurrency.lock: SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the Request row inside the writing transaction (requests.service.ts:848), and FOR UPDATE on the Organization row for nextRequestNumber at create — both unchanged; state-machine invariant 3 extends the first to a client actor without a second mechanism

tasks.title: The notification port — outbox written with the event, delivered after the commit, by an adapter that delivers nothing
tasks.description: Declare `RequestNotifier` as an abstract class used as its own DI token — the shape MailService already uses (apps/api/src/mail/mail.service.ts:152) with its driver chosen in a sibling `*.provider.ts` and registered global, exactly as apps/api/src/mail/mail.provider.ts and core.module.ts do. `deliver(notification)` takes the row's id, organization, request, event action, recipient kind and recipient id and answers a DeliveryOutcome of status delivered|skipped|failed with a channel and optional providerKey/providerRef. `NullRequestNotifier` ships: it marks every row `skipped`, channel `none`, provider key null, and makes no outbound call of any kind. Outbox rows are written IN THE SAME TRANSACTION as the RequestEvent that caused them, one per recipient, for created / status_changed / assignee_changed / message_posted — `field_changed` is not in REQ-03-035's list and notifies nobody. Recipients are the request's requester and the addressee AS THE TRANSACTION LEAVES IT, other than the principal who caused the event, and nobody else: a holder of view-all-requests who is neither receives nothing, and a reassignment therefore notifies the incoming addressee and not the outgoing one. No recipient address is stored anywhere on the row, and `lastError` never holds one. Delivery runs only AFTER the transaction has committed and is not awaited by the route — a slow or hanging provider must never hold a row lock on a request, and a notifier that throws leaves the request, its status and its events exactly as committed with the row at `failed` and `lastError` set. `attempts` is incremented and the provider reference recorded BEFORE the next attempt; a row is retried only from `failed`; the uniqueness constraint means a replayed event can never manufacture a second row. No read path — list, detail, badge — consults the outbox.
allCallSites: apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:534 transition (status_changed for answer, grant, decline, cancel; plus the decline reason's message_posted)

concurrency.lock: none. The insert rides the writing transaction's existing FOR UPDATE on the Request row; the @@unique([eventId, recipientKind, recipientId]) index is the mechanism REQ-03-039 names, and a duplicate insert is rejected by it rather than by a check-then-write

tasks.title: The client's shell — identity, navigation, where sign-in lands, and the requests screens for a client principal
tasks.description: The session gains `principal` and `client` and `role` becomes nullable; nothing renders until the identity endpoint answers, so no member-only navigation is ever painted and then removed. Sidebar: the requests destination is the ONLY organization navigation entry for a client principal — `nav-members` is drawn unconditionally today (Sidebar.tsx:71-77) and is the entry that has to be gated; a destination the caller cannot use is neither drawn nor reachable by typing. Every role-keyed helper on this surface is reached only after the principal kind has been resolved (REQ-03-017): Sidebar.tsx:180, requests/page.tsx:117-119, requests/[requestId]/page.tsx:47-49, requests-badge-context.tsx:41. Post-auth landing: LoginForm.tsx:92 and AcceptInviteScreen.tsx:322 both hardcode `/org/{orgId}/members`, which a client principal is refused; both branch on the principal from `/api/me` — the pattern AcceptInviteScreen already uses — and the login response body is NOT amended, because the contracts amend `/api/me` and leave `POST /api/login` alone. Requests list for a client: no scope control, no vacation section, no control for raising a request, an empty state whose copy does not mention scopes or filters they do not have; the two side reads that would 404 (projects at page.tsx:224, topics at page.tsx:251) are not issued at all. Request detail for a client: the answer, decline, composer and thread controls are drawn and the grant control is not. The screen learns it is the addressee from the principal kind and the fact that the request loaded — every request a client principal can read is one addressed to them (REQ-03-034, REQ-03-029) — because `myMembershipId` comes from the members list ([requestId]/page.tsx:86), which answers a client principal 404. Removed mid-visit: the next call answers 401 and the shell sends them to sign-in; nothing is drawn from a stale response. All components come from `@ds` via apps/web/src/ds.ts, tokens only, no hardcoded colour or size, light theme.

tasks.title: Client detail — the contacts section
tasks.description: A Contacts section below the projects list on client detail, for a contact manager. Ids: client-contacts-section, client-contacts-empty-state, client-contact-invite-btn, client-contact-invite-modal, client-contact-invite-email, client-contact-invite-submit, client-contact-invite-error-email, client-contact-row-{id}, client-contact-row-{id}-remove-btn (drawn while the contact is active). Loading is a skeleton inside the section while the client's own details render behind it. The empty state says what a contact is for and carries the invite control beside it. The submit control shows an in-flight state and is disabled ONLY for the duration of the call — never for validation: clicking an invalid form shows every error and focuses the first invalid field. An address that already contacts a client of the organization keeps the modal open with the error under the field and the typed address intact, and the message is CLIENT_USER_MESSAGES.alreadyLinked from packages/validation, never written inline. `@ds` via apps/web/src/ds.ts, tokens only, light theme.

tasks.title: The new-request modal — the addressee kind, the contact picker, and the per-audience catalogue
tasks.description: Insert the addressee kind above the addressee itself; About, Title, Description, Project, Priority, Needed by and the blocking checkbox keep their positions and their ids. `request-new-assignee-kind` is a `Select` labelled To with two options — NOT a Toggle, which reads as a view switch among labelled fields; `request-new-assignee-client` is a `Select` whose option label is a ReactNode rendering the person's name over their client's, which `1_DS for dev/components/forms/Select.d.ts:3` already types as `React.ReactNode`, so nothing is improvised per screen and there is no DS gap. `request-new-assignee-member` is absent when the client kind is chosen. Choosing the client kind re-reads the catalogue with `audience=client`, clears the chosen topic (a topic of the other audience is one the server will refuse) and keeps title, description, priority, needed-by and blocking; it narrows the project control to projects the requester is assigned to AND that belong to the chosen contact's client, and makes the project required. The narrowings are conveniences — the server decides. When the chosen audience has no active topic the picker is replaced by REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.pickerEmpty and `request-new-submit` is not drawn, evaluated PER AUDIENCE rather than once for the modal; switching back restores both. A failed catalogue read claims nothing: the picker is neither filled nor replaced by the empty copy. `request-new-error-assignee` is new and is shown when no addressee is chosen, with focus moved to the control and the submit control still enabled.

tasks.title: The cases — unit, integration and E2E
tasks.description: Selectors are data-testid only and the ids are the ones the contracts name. Each case references its TC id. The integration suites reach every state through this spec's own product routes and the helpers that already exist — this spec owes NO test fixture and adds nothing under apps/api/src/test-support/. Notifier doubles are registered with `overrideProvider`, the pattern apps/api/test/clients.spec.ts:136 already uses for the mail transport, and reproduce the port's own table of outcomes rather than the spec's prose. TC-03-INT-24 must WAIT for the post-commit drain rather than reading the rows the instant the route answers, because TC-03-INT-26 requires the route to answer before the double is released — the same shape both cases describe. Message assertions quote the Error Messages table literally rather than importing the constant, as apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts already does, so an assertion can fail when the wording drifts. TC-03-E2E-03 mutates the contact's session state and is marked serial. An agent runs the files its diff touches, never the whole suite: `npm test -- test/client-participants.spec.ts` from apps/api, and `E2E_WEB_PORT=3100 E2E_API_PORT=4100 CI=1 npx playwright test tests/client-participants.spec.ts tests/regressions.spec.ts` from e2e. `e2e/tests/app-shell.spec.ts:22` asserts `nav-members` for an admin and is the regression witness that gating it did not remove the row for staff.

sections.Summary: no task — orientation. The two things it introduces, the ClientMembership principal and the notification port, are T1/T3/T4 and T6.
sections.Actors & Preconditions: T3, T4 — the client contact and the contact manager are the two new callers; T5 restates the requester's precondition (assigned to the project) as REQ-03-023.
sections.Roles & Permission Matrix: T2, T3 — the matrix itself is in the contracts file and adds no role, no staff capability and no matrix column; the client column is the flat CLIENT_CAPABILITIES list resolved from the principal kind.
sections.Functional Requirements: T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9 — every REQ-03-001…042 is assigned to at least one task.
sections.State Machine: T4 (the contact's own lifecycle and its transition table), T5 (invariant 3 — every status write re-reads the row FOR UPDATE and tests the actor guard against that read, whichever principal kind the actor is), T3/T4 (invariant 1, enforced at both writes by REQ-03-014 and REQ-03-042, never by the schema).
sections.Out of Scope: no task — six exclusions. A client raising a request is refused by REQ-03-027 (T5); actual mail and per-contact preferences are a later adapter spec (T6 ships the port and nothing that sends); a contact belonging to more than one client or organization, client-side attachments, a client seeing tasks/time/reports, and self-service sign-up are built nowhere and no route admits them.
sections.Known Gaps: no task — five accepted gaps, each one a thing deliberately not built: no delivery, no reassignment of a removed contact's requests, no separately designed client shell, the contact's address visible to view-clients holders, and delivery attempted only while the API is being called. Nothing here asks for code.
sections.Acceptance Criteria: T10 — all 17 criteria are observed by the cases named in the Observed-by column, and every one of those cases is claimed above.
sections.Routes: T3, T4, T5 — the guard chain, the success codes and the error bodies of every amended and every new route.
sections.Error Messages: T2 — every row is placed in `messages` below with its module and the route that emits it.
sections.The notification port: T6 — the port's members, its two adapters and the retry policy.
sections.Validation Rules: T2 (the client half of rules 1, 5, 8, 13), T4 (rules 2, 3, 4), T5 (rules 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12) — the server re-validates every rule and the server-only ones have no client-side half at all.
sections.Screens: T8 (the contacts section), T9 (the modal with a client addressee), T7 (what a client contact sees).
sections.UI Description: T7, T8, T9 — every surface row.
sections.DS gaps: no task — the spec records NONE, and both controls in doubt are built from primitives apps/web/src/ds.ts already exports; `dsGaps` below is empty and anything found missing during implementation goes INTO the design system, never improvised per screen.
sections.Security: T3 (the 404 discipline and the ordering that keeps the role-keyed helpers unreachable), T4 (revocation through securityStamp), T5 (request existence not enumerable), T6 (no address stored, none in lastError) — the spec adds no unauthenticated route of its own.
sections.Verification Plan: T10 — the rig is walked through this spec's own routes and the existing helpers; no fixture is owed.

risks.risk: REQ-03-019 is enforced at OrgScopeGuard, which every organization route in the product passes through. A mistake there refuses staff everywhere, and the failure is loud but total.
risks.mitigation: the refusal is keyed on the resolved principal being `client` and nothing else, the seven exempt handlers opt in explicitly so a new route fails closed, and TC-03-INT-13 asserts the admin call still answers 200 beside every client 404 — the 404 is about the principal, not about the route being broken.

risks.risk: The dispatcher runs after every request-mutating call. Awaiting it would make a hanging provider hold the route, and not awaiting it makes TC-03-INT-24's assertion racy.
risks.mitigation: dispatch is scheduled after the commit and is not awaited (TC-03-INT-26), and TC-03-INT-24 waits for the drain rather than reading the instant the route answers. With the shipped adapter there is no I/O at all.

risks.risk: A decline writes two events in one transaction (message_posted and status_changed), so reading REQ-03-035 per event produces two outbox rows per recipient for one decline. No case asserts the count.
risks.mitigation: planned as the spec's own words say — one row per recipient per notifiable RequestEvent, with field_changed notifying nobody — and recorded as note N1 for a person.

risks.risk: The request detail screen learns who the caller is from GET …/members, which a client principal is refused, so the answer and decline controls would not be drawn.
risks.mitigation: for a client principal the members read is not issued at all and the addressee test is the fact that the request loaded — REQ-03-034 makes every readable request theirs. No new endpoint field is invented.

risks.risk: LoginForm and AcceptInviteScreen both hardcode /org/{orgId}/members, which a contact cannot reach, so a signed-in contact would land on a 404.
risks.mitigation: both branch on the principal from /api/me, which the contracts do amend; POST /api/login's body is left exactly as it is, since the contracts do not amend it.

risks.risk: Gating nav-members could remove the row for staff, which no case in this spec would catch.
risks.mitigation: e2e/tests/app-shell.spec.ts:22 already asserts nav-members for an admin and is the regression witness; TC-03-E2E-02 asserts the admin's sidebar draws members, projects and clients beside the contact's, so the absence is proven to be the principal's.

risks.risk: A client principal can still reach /account/settings, which is not an organization route and which this spec does not gate.
risks.mitigation: the page resolves /api/me and renders the shell, whose navigation is now the requests entry alone, and the account routes carry no organization scope, so nothing about the staff product is exposed. Recorded here rather than silently assumed.
